advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert or set restrictive (0o700) permissions on any intermediate parent directories created by _artifact_dir's mkdir(parents=True), not only the leaf.
evidence: _assert_private_artifact_dir only checks the passed leaf path: `if stat.S_IMODE(mode) & 0o077:` (line 266)
docs/comment-echo-reclaim-runbook.md: 'It contains sensitive Jira material and rollback capability; mode it 0700'
advisory.finding: _artifact_dir creates the artifact directory with mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True), but any intermediate parent directories are created with the default (umask-derived) mode and are never permission-checked; only the leaf directory is asserted to lack 0o077 bits. The runbook states this directory holds sensitive Jira material and rollback capability and must be mode 0700.
advisory.suggested_fix: Require the parent to already exist (drop parents=True) or verify/tighten each created parent's mode; alternatively require an operator-created 0700 directory and refuse to auto-create it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a cleanup test that resumes `run()` from a journal ending in `delete_outcome(ambiguous, target_present)` and asserts exactly one further DELETE attempt on the still-present target plus the resulting outcome/after-state.
evidence: test_ambiguous_retained_target_is_journaled_and_stops_without_retry produces exactly the journal `[('delete_intent',None,None),('delete_outcome','ambiguous','target_present')]` (tests/integration/test_cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:507-510) but never re-invokes `run()` on that artifact directory
search of tests/integration/test_cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py for 'retryable' returned no matches — the retryable resume state has no assertion

Existing restart tests only cover the `unresolved` state (test_restart_recovers_intent_after_delete, lines 554-602) and the crash-before-outcome six-action case (test_restart_resumes_six_action_canary, lines 744-788)
advisory.finding: The cleanup state machine's `retryable` resume branch is never exercised: a persisted journal ending in `delete_outcome(ambiguous/recovered, observed_state='target_present')` makes `_journal_progress` return `"retryable"`, which routes `run()` into the else branch and re-attempts a DELETE from `completed_count`. No test resumes a run from that journal, so the resume-after-retained-target path (and its at-most-one-additional-attempt / postcondition behavior) is untested.
scenarios: A quiet-window operator gets an ambiguous DELETE whose target remained, the tool stops with a persisted retryable outcome, and the operator reruns the same digest-confirmed command to resume.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that (1) runs execute against AmbiguousBeforeDeleteJira to persist the retryable journal, then (2) re-runs execute with a normal FakeJira and asserts the single additional delete_call, the final journal shape, and jira-after.json contents.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly os.chmod the created artifact directory to 0o700 after mkdir so its mode does not depend on the ambient umask.
evidence: Python's Path.mkdir mode is combined with the process umask, so the resulting mode is 0o700 & ~umask
dropped.finding: mkdir(mode=0o700) is subject to the process umask; on the extremely rare umask that clears owner bits this could produce an unusable directory, but more relevantly the mode argument does not guarantee exactly 0o700 without an explicit chmod. The subsequent _assert_private_artifact_dir only rejects group/world bits, so a stricter-than-expected or umask-narrowed mode is tolerated; this is acceptable but the reliance on umask for the security-relevant mode is implicit and undocumented in code.
